evidence: src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) is used in write() via this.prisma.visitNote.create, but notesFor() does `const prisma = new PrismaClient();` and skips the injected abstraction

src/business/services/SchedulingService.ts: depends on PatientDao/AppointmentDao and turns rows into Patient/Practitioner/Appointment entities, while VisitNotesService works on raw Prisma rows: two different data-access styles in one module
src/business/services/SchedulingService.ts: `new Appointment(a.id, a.patientId, a.practitionerId, a.startsAt, a.minutes, a.status as AppointmentStatus)` is repeated in book() and cancel()
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit fails, mainly because of VisitNotesService.ts. Both services cover the appointment domain, but they use the module's abstractions in different ways. SchedulingService takes DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao) and turns rows into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment) before applying rules. VisitNotesService takes PrismaService and works directly on Prisma rows, with no entity. It also undercuts its own abstraction: write() uses the injected this.prisma, but notesFor() creates its own `new PrismaClient()`, skipping the injected PrismaService. That bypass breaks the rubric. There is also duplication. The row-to-VisitNote mapping is written out twice in VisitNotesService. In SchedulingService, the row-to-Appointment conversion (`new Appointment(a.id, a.patientId, a.practitionerId, a.startsAt, a.minutes, a.status as AppointmentStatus)`) is repeated in book() and cancel(), so the mapping rule lives in two places.

violations.message: notesFor() creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected PrismaService (this.prisma), skipping the module's own data-access abstraction that write() uses.
Works directly on Prisma rows with no domain entity, unlike SchedulingService's DAO-plus-entity approach. The row-to-VisitNote mapping is also written separately in write() and notesFor().
The row-to-Appointment conversion (`new Appointment(a.id, ..., a.status as AppointmentStatus)`) is repeated in book() and cancel() instead of living in one place.
